properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, AND DELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON. Anthony, 2026-08-19: *"let's capture the feedback, but hold off on tackling anything from it — your context is getting high, so let's tackle them in the next session."* **Nothing here has been built.** Full text: `art:ophyd-service-feedback-2026-08-19`, `art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-08-19` — REGISTERED Artifacts, PARKED under the accepted `dec:a-dated-field-report-is-registered-and-parked`, files at `docs/feedback/2026-08-19-*-agent-feedback.md`. They correctly attach to nothing and `parks` is how the design says so; an earlier pass in this session deleted them instead, on the mistaken argument that no honest edge existed — see `dec:idea-parks-shipped-and-was-still-not-reached-the-instruction-is-missing-where-the-person-is-stuck`.

Two agents, two of his work projects, filed independently on the same day. **Neither complains about the MODEL.** ophyd's own summary: *"The friction list is almost entirely about write ergonomics on long-lived nodes, not about the model."*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ VERIFIED BEFORE RECORDING — three checks run this session

**1. THE ITEM GRADED "worst one" DOES NOT REPRODUCE.** ophyd reports `add_decision` upsert silently resetting an accepted Decision to `proposed`. Tested on 0.36.0 at BOTH layers, checking BOTH the reply and the stored value: status survives. `upsert_node` reads existing properties, extends with supplied, writes — the merge is correct. A second hypothesis (that a REFUSED call still mutates) was also tested and is wrong: the dedup guard correctly does not fire on your own existing node, so the call simply succeeds. 🛑 **Either it is already fixed, or that session ran a stale binary — and MERGED-≠-SERVED bit this very session twice. ASK WHAT VERSION THEIR SERVER REPORTED before anything is built.**

**2. THE SKILL-NAME DRIFT IS REAL, confirmed by inspection.** EIGHT advertised commands have no skill of that name: `rules`, `req`, `gaps`, `decisions`, `where`, `kpp`, `health`, `debt`. `get_skill('rules')` correctly refuses and lists 20 names, none of them `rules`. ⭐ **reflow2 already owns the doctrine that fixes it** — `req:a-refusal-names-what-would-have-worked` — the refusal simply does not map aliases. *"'rules' is served as 'governance-proposal'"* is the whole change.

**3. `description` UNDECLARED ON `ChangeEvent` IS REPORTED BY BOTH PROJECTS INDEPENDENTLY.** hxm's framing is the sharper one: the flag fires on **every legitimate write**, which **trains the caller to ignore `undeclared`** and defeats its typo-catching purpose. One schema line.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ THREE ITEMS THIS SESSION CORROBORATES FIRST-HAND, from a third project (reflow2 itself)

· **PROMOTION ALWAYS TRIPS THE DEDUP GUARD** (ophyd #5). Hit on EVERY promotion today — decision→requirement→capability, `distinct_from` boilerplate each time. Their fix — a `promotes: <decision-id>` parameter that draws a real edge, skips the guard, and gives the Decision its road-taken link for free — **turns friction into structure**. Three projects now.
· **EVOLVING A LONG DECISION MEANS RESENDING ALL OF IT** (ophyd #2). Multi-thousand-word bodies resent repeatedly today, each with the revision block warning the prior text exists only in the reply. **The riskiest write pattern in the tool.** Their `resolve_decision(id, resolution_text, status)` would remove friction #1 and #2 together.
· **APPEND-ONLY EDITS GET THE MAXIMUM-ALARM REVISION NOTE** (hxm #3). Same experience. Their fix is right: a diff-aware *"new value strictly extends the prior"* **preserves the alarm's signal for the genuinely destructive case.**

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE BIGGEST ITEM IS NOT A BUG — "reflow2 AS A PROGRAM BRAIN, NOT A PROJECT BRAIN"

Anthony's own framing, quoted by the agent: *"kind of a strange way to be using reflow2… managing this scattered 'project' that has multiple facets, but that are all inter-related."* Five repos, two people, a simulated beamline, a PR pipeline, one graph, three days of heavy load.

**Its central claim: the ontology ALREADY FITS.** Capabilities outliving any repo, Contributors with authorship and ownership, Verifications naming a beamline session rather than a CI job, epochs, releases, TRL/MRL gates — *"that vocabulary is program-shaped. The single-system framing lives mostly in adopt/genesis's front door, not in the schema."*

TWO NAMED STRAINS:
· **People-readiness has no node type.** The program's real gate includes *"AJ can independently build and maintain this stack"*, and readiness modelling stops at technologies. The learning ladder got smuggled into a TemporalFact's context sentence.
· **Facet-blind interrogation.** Writing 12 advisory craft rules moved unsurfaced gaps 7 → 19: the gap engine prices a craft-of-practice rule identically to a system requirement. 📌 This is the SAME SHAPE as `dec:idea-a-project-says-what-it-is-doing-now-so-the-loop-stops-pushing`, settled today — the loop asking the right question at the wrong moment — arriving from a different direction.

📌 THEIR SUGGESTION: name the use case in the docs, and have genesis/adopt **ask "system or program?" up front instead of assuming system.**

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
THE REST, UNRANKED AND UNJUDGED (see the artifacts for full text)

ophyd: review/ack records swamp `scan_nodes(Decision)` (~40 of 61); loop-debt classes have no acknowledge path, so a deliberate state keeps the loop from ever reading clean and it is unclear whether `ruling: parks` covers it; three tools needed to see all debt; token weight of `get_skill` and `propagate_change`; the `create_node`-vs-`add_*` scar tissue.
ophyd ideas: `resolve_decision`; promotion edges as first-class; a one-call `demonstration` record for *"X was seen working live on DATE in ENV"* (the commonest evidence at a beamline, currently 3 loads + 3 calls); a session-scoped write journal.
hxm: ChangeEvent `name` has no length steer; **a "sighting" mechanism for DesignRules** — ⭐ which `fact:the-gh-merge-failure-is-snap-confinement-and-nobody-was-counting` shows arriving independently from a second direction the same day; `get_skill` batch or ETag.

⚠️ NOTHING HERE IS PRIORITISED YET, and the ordering above is exposition, not a plan. The two cheapest CONFIRMED items are the `ChangeEvent.description` declaration and the alias-mapping refusal.
properties.name: OPEN — two more projects filed field reports the same day: the friction is almost entirely WRITE ERGONOMICS ON LONG-LIVED NODES, and one of them says reflow2 is being used as a PROGRAM brain, not a project brain
properties.rationale: Captured on Anthony's instruction to record the feedback and defer the work to a fresh session, so nothing is lost to context pressure and nothing is half-built. The three verification results are recorded ahead of the reports themselves because they change what should be built: the item its own author graded worst does not reproduce and may be a stale-binary artefact, which would misdirect a whole increment if taken at face value; and two other items are confirmed rather than merely reported. This session's own first-hand corroboration of three friction items is included because reflow2 is effectively a third reporting project, and three independent hits on the promotion guard is a different weight of evidence from one. The program-brain observation is given its own section rather than filed among the friction because it is a claim about what reflow2 IS, and its author argues the schema already supports it while the front-door skills do not.
